paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan son of Yitzchak son of Acha.
He is mentioned at the beginning of Peah chapter 5 and in Shekalim 1:2. In his commentary on Peah, Rabbi Shimshon of Sens reads “Rabbi Yochanan.”

notes.text: The specific commentator behind ר״ש remains unverified here. The Yonatan/Yochanan variant remains attributed to that Peah commentary.

The original research selector yields only ג and cannot support its claimed chain. The corrected selector in the same saved Guggenheimer Peah 5:1 raw response explicitly has Yonatan, son of Yitzchak bar Acha. The saved Vilna Rash MiShantz commentary on Mishnah Peah 5:1:5 quotes Yochanan bar Yitzchak bar Acha, supporting the commentator expansion and reported variant. This supersedes the earlier uncertainty about that commentator only; all carried notes remain archived. The variant and source questions are preserved without authority or genealogical admission.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 702) cites Shekalim 1:2 (ה״ב), where the supplied text has 1:3 (ה״ג). In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 1:2 and Peah 5:1 both name Rabbi Yonatan son of Yitzchak bar Acha in the discussion of intercalation. The consulted Rash MiShantz on Mishnah Peah 5:1 quotes Rabbi Yochanan bar Yitzchak bar Acha in that passage.
